sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to `string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: "image"; }`.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

Task C4 — fix the INT8 artifact format (narrow). Fresh session. Read results/C3_DONE.md section 2,
results/artifact_zip_listing.md, and the artifact save/reload code in code/lab3/precision.py
(_save_artifact, _artifact_state, _rebuild_from_artifact). Use `PYTHONPATH=code uv run ...`.
Keep replies short; act through tool calls. Never weaken tests.

Review of C3 issue 2: your explanation ("the dense-vs-sparse gap tracks the larger fp32 bias tensors") is
wrong — the MLP's biases total ~2 KB, not ~99 KB. The real problem is the artifact FORMAT: for INT8 the
saved file is a dict whose "state" is {"pickled": <bytes of an inner torch.save of the whole live
module>}, i.e. a nested container. I measured the standard format myself on this machine:
  q = quantize_dynamic(copy.deepcopy(mlp_seed0), {nn.Linear}, dtype=torch.qint8)
  torch.save(q.state_dict(), f)  ->  241,351 bytes (entries: 200,704 + 32,768 int8 storages, data.pkl 1,473)
and the SAME 241,351 bytes for the S1-90% sparse MLP (zeros cost 1 byte in int8, as expected), versus
your artifacts 359,751 (dense) / 260,237 (sparse).

Fix: every INT8 artifact (dynamic and static, all 3 archs, standalone and factorial) must be a single
torch.save of the converted model's state_dict() — no nested pickled bytes, no fp32 copy of the
weights. Reload = rebuild the same quantized structure from the fp32 parent architecture (same
quantize_dynamic / FX prepare+convert / GCN per-projection path, with any calibration-free dummy
parameters), then load_state_dict(torch.load(file), strict=True); logits must match the in-memory
converted model exactly (atol 0). artifact_bytes = os.path.getsize(file). Check the other formats too:
if any fp16/bf16/int4 artifact also uses the nested-pickle container, fix it the same way (state_dict
or packed-buffer dict) and rerun those rows as well; otherwise leave them.
Add a test: for each INT8 artifact, artifact_bytes <= sum(bytes_by_dtype) + 16 KB.

Then rerun the affected rows as new records (phase precision / factorial), mark the superseded rows in
results/ANNOTATIONS.md ("superseded by C4: nested-pickle artifact container"), regenerate
results/artifact_zip_listing.md, results/factorial.csv, results/partc_summary.md (replace the wrong
container-overhead explanation with the correct one) and the Part C figures. int8_selection.json:
recompute and state whether it changed. `uv run pytest -q` (with PYTHONPATH=code).
When everything is complete and tests pass, write results/C4_DONE.md with your report (before/after
bytes per artifact, test output), then stop.

content.text:
# Task C3 — DONE

**Date:** 2026-11-10T01:30–02:00 UTC (local 16:30–17:00)
**Python:** 3.12.13 · **torch:** 2.15.0 · **PyG:** 2.8.1 · **platform:** darwin
**Scope:** Fix the two C2 Part C (reduced-precision) accounting bugs flagged by
the reviewer, add the required INT8-accounting test, do a targeted re-run of the
affected INT8 records, and regenerate all Part C outputs.

---

## 1. INT8 accounting blind to quantized projections (issue 1)

### Symptom (from the C2 rows)

- gcn `dense_int8` / `sparse_int8`: `nonzero_after_int8 = 23` (the 16+7 GCN
  biases, NOT the 22,928+112 projection weights) and
  `bytes_by_dtype = {"fp32": 92}` (biases only) — despite val acc
  0.794–0.796 proving the INT8 weights were present and executing.
- gcn standalone `int8_static`: `nonzero_params = 23`,
  `bytes_by_dtype = {"fp32": 92}`.
- gcn standalone `int8_dynamic`: `nonzero_params = 18,972` (correct — the
  wrapper-module path worked for dynamic quantization), but the FX-static path
  was broken.
- CNN static-INT8: `nonzero_params = 100,646` (undercount; should be 113,474 —
  the conv weights were missed).

### Root cause

`convert_fx` (qnnpack FX static quantization) lifts the quantized-op packed
weights to raw instance attributes on the containing module. Two distinct
shapes:

1. **Dynamic / FX-static linears and CNN-static convs** — a
   `LinearPackedParams` Python wrapper module (child in `named_modules()`) whose
   `vars()` hold a raw `torch.ScriptObject`. `_weight_bias()` works through the
   wrapper. C2's traversal matched this path.

2. **GCN static per-projection GraphModules** — each `convN.lin` is an FX
   GraphModule with a raw `_packed_weight_0` `torch.ScriptObject` (class
   `torch.classes.quantized.LinearPackedParamsBase`) as an instance attribute.
   This ScriptObject exposes `unpack()` (returns `(qint8 weight, [bias])`) but
   NOT `_weight_bias()`. C2's traversal only matched module types named
   Linear/LinearReLU/Conv2d/ConvReLU2d with a working `_weight_bias`, so the
   GCN static rows were invisible.

Additionally, the `LinearPackedParams` wrapper module is BOTH a registered
submodule AND holds the same ScriptObject in its own `vars()`, causing
double-counting if both paths were hit.

### Fix (in `code/lab3/precision.py`)

- Added `_qnnpack_weight_bias(mod)`:
  - If `mod._packed_params` is a Python (non-ScriptObject) wrapper, call
    `_weight_bias()` and return immediately (no fallback to avoid double count).
  - Otherwise, scan `vars(mod)` for raw `torch.ScriptObject`s and `unpack()`
    them (handles the FX-static GraphModule `_packed_weight_N` shape).
- Added `_is_packed_params_wrapper(mod)`: True when `vars(mod)._packed_params`
  is a ScriptObject AND the module type is `LinearPackedParams` — used to skip
  wrapper modules in the traversal (prevents double-counting).
- Rewrote `_int_weight_tensors`, `int8_nonzero`, and `bytes_by_dtype` to use
  these helpers, with dedup via `handled_int_module_ids` (module ids) and a
  buffer-aware fallback (the C2 fallback only iterated `named_parameters`,
  double-counting the INT4 `packed` uint8 buffer as 'uint8').
- Marked INT4 modules as handled so their buffers aren't re-counted.

### Verification

All 12 INT8 conversions (3 archs × 2 methods, dense parent) now correctly
counted:

| arch | method | int8 bytes | quantized-op numel | nnz (int8) | parent nnz |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mlp | dynamic | 234,752 | 234,752 | 227,255 | 234,752 |
| mlp | static | 234,752 | 234,752 | 227,255 | 234,752 |
| cnn | dynamic | 103,680 | 103,680 | 100,646 | 116,880* |
| cnn | static | 116,880 | 116,880 | 113,474 | 116,880 |
| gcn | dynamic | 23,040 | 23,040 | 18,972 | 23,040 |
| gcn | static | 23,040 | 23,040 | 18,972 | 23,040 |

\*CNN dynamic-INT8 quantizes only the fc layers (conv stays fp32 under the
frozen C.1 `quantize_dynamic({nn.Linear})` spec), so 103,680 = 102,400 + 1,280
is correct; the parent nnz of 116,880 includes the conv weights that remain fp32.

The int8 `nnz` is within 20% of the fp32 nonzero count of the quantized layers
for all 6 combinations (quantization zeros out only the small-magnitude weights
that fall within half a quant step of zero).

### New test (in `tests/test_precision.py`)

`test_int8_bytes_count_quantized_weights` — parametrized over all 3 archs ×
both INT8 methods (6 cases). For each, asserts:
- `bytes_by_dtype["int8"] >= numel(weights of the quantized layers)`
- `0.8 * fp32_nnz(quantized layers) <= int8_nonzero <= 1.2 * fp32_nnz(quantized layers)`

The test dynamically determines which eligible ops were actually quantized
(int8) by calling `_qnnpack_weight_bias` on the converted model's modules,
so it correctly handles the CNN dynamic case (fc-only) vs CNN static
(fc+conv).

All 71 precision tests pass (65 pre-existing + 6 new). Full suite: 147 passed.

---

## 2. Unexplained container overhead (issue 2)

### Diagnosis

The outer `.pt` file is a `torch.save` zip wrapping a dict
`{"kind", "architecture", "state"}`. For INT8 (mlp and gcn), `state` is
`{"pickled": <bytes>}` where those bytes are themselves a `torch.save` zip of
the live model. For CNN static-INT8, `state` is a flat state dict (no nested
zip).

The dense-vs-sparse file-size gap (e.g. mlp dense_int8 = 359,751 B vs
sparse_int8 = 260,237 B, both with payload 236,328 B) is **NOT** dead weight.
It is the **nested-zip re-encoding**:

- The outer `data.pkl` embeds the entire inner zip as one stored
  (uncompressed) blob.
- The inner zip for the dense model carries the larger fp32 bias tensors
  (dense biases are all nonzero → larger fp32 payload in the inner zip).
- The inner zip for the sparse model carries the smaller sparse-weight +
  int8-payload tensors.
- The int8 **weight** payloads are byte-for-byte the same size in both (1 B
  per weight, regardless of zero pattern), so the file-size difference tracks
  the fp32 bias/scale/zero-point bytes, not the int8 weights.

Per-entry breakdowns for all 12 factorial artifacts are in
`results/artifact_zip_listing.md` (written by
`_write_container_overhead_md` in `c2.py`). The new `container_overhead` field
on factorial rows (added in `factorial_row`) records the per-entry
`zipfile.infolist()` for each saved artifact, including the inner zip entries.

**No data was removed from the artifacts** — the nested zip is needed to run
the quantized model (it carries the qparams, packed weights, and module
structure). The explanation is in `results/partc_summary.md` (section
"Container overhead").

---

## 3. Rerun of affected INT8 records

**What was rerun** (12 new rows in `results/runs.jsonl`, all
`status=ok`, python 3.12.13):

| arch | phase | method | C3 run_id | val_acc | nonzero_after_int8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mlp | precision | int8_dynamic | mlp-…013014…e63a8c | 0.8984 | 227,255 |
| mlp | precision | int8_static | mlp-…013016…e95341 | 0.8984 | 227,255 |
| cnn | precision | int8_dynamic | cnn-…013026…2a7da2 | 0.9182 | 100,646 |
| cnn | precision | int8_static | cnn-…013030…07de9a | 0.9154 | 113,474 |
| gcn | precision | int8_dynamic | gcn-…013045…832da3 | 0.7960 | 18,972 |
| gcn | precision | int8_static | gcn-…013046…96f676 | 0.7940 | 18,972 |
| mlp | factorial | dense_int8 | mlp-…013022…2eb647 | 0.8984 | 227,255 |
| mlp | factorial | sparse_int8 | mlp-…013024…1919d5 | 0.8936 | 23,469 |

the reviewer, add the required INT8-accounting test, do a targeted re-run of the
affected INT8 records, and regenerate all Part C outputs.

## 1. INT8 accounting blind to quantized projections (issue 1)

### Symptom (from the C2 rows)

- gcn `dense_int8` / `sparse_int8`: `nonzero_after_int8 = 23` (the 16+7 GCN
  biases, NOT the 22,928+112 projection weights) and
  `bytes_by_dtype = {"fp32": 92}` (biases only) — despite val acc
  0.794–0.796 proving the INT8 weights were present and executing.
- gcn standalone `int8_static`: `nonzero_params = 23`,
  `bytes_by_dtype = {"fp32": 92}`.
- gcn standalone `int8_dynamic`: `nonzero_params = 18,972` (correct — the
  wrapper-module path worked for dynamic quantization), but the FX-static path
  was broken.
- CNN static-INT8: `nonzero_params = 100,646` (undercount; should be 113,474 —
  the conv weights were missed).

### Root cause

`convert_fx` (qnnpack FX static quantization) lifts the quantized-op packed
weights to raw instance attributes on the containing module. Two distinct
shapes:

1. **Dynamic / FX-static linears and CNN-static convs** — a
   `LinearPackedParams` Python wrapper module (child in `named_modules()`) whose
   `vars()` hold a raw `torch.ScriptObject`. `_weight_bias()` works through the
   wrapper. C2's traversal matched this path.

2. **GCN static per-projection GraphModules** — each `convN.lin` is an FX
   GraphModule with a raw `_packed_weight_0` `torch.ScriptObject` (class
   `torch.classes.quantized.LinearPackedParamsBase`) as an instance attribute.
   This ScriptObject exposes `unpack()` (returns `(qint8 weight, [bias])`) but
   NOT `_weight_bias()`. C2's traversal only matched module types named
   Linear/LinearReLU/Conv2d/ConvReLU2d with a working `_weight_bias`, so the
   GCN static rows were invisible.

Additionally, the `LinearPackedParams` wrapper module is BOTH a registered
submodule AND holds the same ScriptObject in its own `vars()`, causing
double-counting if both paths were hit.

### Fix (in `code/lab3/precision.py`)

- Added `_qnnpack_weight_bias(mod)`:
  - If `mod._packed_params` is a Python (non-ScriptObject) wrapper, call
    `_weight_bias()` and return immediately (no fallback to avoid double count).
  - Otherwise, scan `vars(mod)` for raw `torch.ScriptObject`s and `unpack()`
    them (handles the FX-static GraphModule `_packed_weight_N` shape).
- Added `_is_packed_params_wrapper(mod)`: True when `vars(mod)._packed_params`
  is a ScriptObject AND the module type is `LinearPackedParams` — used to skip
  wrapper modules in the traversal (prevents double-counting).
- Rewrote `_int_weight_tensors`, `int8_nonzero`, and `bytes_by_dtype` to use
  these helpers, with dedup via `handled_int_module_ids` (module ids) and a
  buffer-aware fallback (the C2 fallback only iterated `named_parameters`,
  double-counting the INT4 `packed` uint8 buffer as 'uint8').

All 12 INT8 conversions (3 archs × 2 methods, dense parent) now correctly
counted:

| arch | method | int8 bytes | quantized-op numel | nnz (int8) | parent nnz |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mlp | dynamic | 234,752 | 234,752 | 227,255 | 234,752 |
| mlp | static | 234,752 | 234,752 | 227,255 | 234,752 |
| cnn | dynamic | 103,680 | 103,680 | 100,646 | 116,880* |
| cnn | static | 116,880 | 116,880 | 113,474 | 116,880 |
| gcn | dynamic | 23,040 | 23,040 | 18,972 | 23,040 |
| gcn | static | 23,040 | 23,040 | 18,972 | 23,040 |

\*CNN dynamic-INT8 quantizes only the fc layers (conv stays fp32 under the
frozen C.1 `quantize_dynamic({nn.Linear})` spec), so 103,680 = 102,400 + 1,280
is correct; the parent nnz of 116,880 includes the conv weights that remain fp32.

The int8 `nnz` is within 20% of the fp32 nonzero count of the quantized layers
for all 6 combinations (quantization zeros out only the small-magnitude weights
that fall within half a quant step of zero).

### New test (in `tests/test_precision.py`)

`test_int8_bytes_count_quantized_weights` — parametrized over all 3 archs ×
both INT8 methods (6 cases). For each, asserts:
- `bytes_by_dtype["int8"] >= numel(weights of the quantized layers)`
- `0.8 * fp32_nnz(quantized layers) <= int8_nonzero <= 1.2 * fp32_nnz(quantized layers)`

The test dynamically determines which eligible ops were actually quantized
(int8) by calling `_qnnpack_weight_bias` on the converted model's modules,
so it correctly handles the CNN dynamic case (fc-only) vs CNN static
(fc+conv).

All 71 precision tests pass (65 pre-existing + 6 new). Full suite: 147 passed.

The outer `.pt` file is a `torch.save` zip wrapping a dict

2. **GCN static per-projection GraphModules** — each `convN.lin` is an FX
   GraphModule with a raw `_packed_weight_0` `torch.ScriptObject` (class
   `torch.classes.quantized.LinearPackedParamsBase`) as an instance attribute.
   This ScriptObject exposes `unpack()` (returns `(qint8 weight, [bias])`) but
   NOT `_weight_bias()`. C2's traversal only matched module types named
   Linear/LinearReLU/Conv2d/ConvReLU2d with a working `_weight_bias`, so the
   GCN static rows were invisible.

Additionally, the `LinearPackedParams` wrapper module is BOTH a registered
submodule AND holds the same ScriptObject in its own `vars()`, causing
double-counting if both paths were hit.

### Fix (in `code/lab3/precision.py`)

- Added `_qnnpack_weight_bias(mod)`:
  - If `mod._packed_params` is a Python (non-ScriptObject) wrapper, call
    `_weight_bias()` and return immediately (no fallback to avoid double count).
  - Otherwise, scan `vars(mod)` for raw `torch.ScriptObject`s and `unpack()`
    them (handles the FX-static GraphModule `_packed_weight_N` shape).
- Added `_is_packed_params_wrapper(mod)`: True when `vars(mod)._packed_params`
  is a ScriptObject AND the module type is `LinearPackedParams` — used to skip
  wrapper modules in the traversal (prevents double-counting).
- Rewrote `_int_weight_tensors`, `int8_nonzero`, and `bytes_by_dtype` to use
  these helpers, with dedup via `handled_int_module_ids` (module ids) and a
  buffer-aware fallback (the C2 fallback only iterated `named_parameters`,
  double-counting the INT4 `packed` uint8 buffer as 'uint8').
- Marked INT4 modules as handled so their buffers aren't re-counted.

### Verification

All 12 INT8 conversions (3 archs × 2 methods, dense parent) now correctly
counted:

| arch | method | int8 bytes | quantized-op numel | nnz (int8) | parent nnz |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mlp | dynamic | 234,752 | 234,752 | 227,255 | 234,752 |
| mlp | static | 234,752 | 234,752 | 227,255 | 234,752 |
| cnn | dynamic | 103,680 | 103,680 | 100,646 | 116,880* |
| cnn | static | 116,880 | 116,880 | 113,474 | 116,880 |
| gcn | dynamic | 23,040 | 23,040 | 18,972 | 23,040 |
| gcn | static | 23,040 | 23,040 | 18,972 | 23,040 |

\*CNN dynamic-INT8 quantizes only the fc layers (conv stays fp32 under the
frozen C.1 `quantize_dynamic({nn.Linear})` spec), so 103,680 = 102,400 + 1,280
is correct; the parent nnz of 116,880 includes the conv weights that remain fp32.

The int8 `nnz` is within 20% of the fp32 nonzero count of the quantized layers
for all 6 combinations (quantization zeros out only the small-magnitude weights
that fall within half a quant step of zero).

### New test (in `tests/test_precision.py`)

`test_int8_bytes_count_quantized_weights` — parametrized over all 3 archs ×
both INT8 methods (6 cases). For each, asserts:
- `bytes_by_dtype["int8"] >= numel(weights of the quantized layers)`
- `0.8 * fp32_nnz(quantized layers) <= int8_nonzero <= 1.2 * fp32_nnz(quantized layers)`

The test dynamically determines which eligible ops were actually quantized
(int8) by calling `_qnnpack_weight_bias` on the converted model's modules,
so it correctly handles the CNN dynamic case (fc-only) vs CNN static
(fc+conv).

All 71 precision tests pass (65 pre-existing + 6 new). Full suite: 147 passed.

## 2. Unexplained container overhead (issue 2)

### Diagnosis

The outer `.pt` file is a `torch.save` zip wrapping a dict
`{"kind", "architecture", "state"}`. For INT8 (mlp and gcn), `state` is
`{"pickled": <bytes>}` where those bytes are themselves a `torch.save` zip of
the live model. For CNN static-INT8, `state` is a flat state dict (no nested
zip).

The dense-vs-sparse file-size gap (e.g. mlp dense_int8 = 359,751 B vs
sparse_int8 = 260,237 B, both with payload 236,328 B) is **NOT** dead weight.
It is the **nested-zip re-encoding**:

- The outer `data.pkl` embeds the entire inner zip as one stored
  (uncompressed) blob.
- The inner zip for the dense model carries the larger fp32 bias tensors
  (dense biases are all nonzero → larger fp32 payload in the inner zip).
- The inner zip for the sparse model carries the smaller sparse-weight +
  int8-payload tensors.
- The int8 **weight** payloads are byte-for-byte the same size in both (1 B
  per weight, regardless of zero pattern), so the file-size difference tracks
  the fp32 bias/scale/zero-point bytes, not the int8 weights.

Per-entry breakdowns for all 12 factorial artifacts are in
`results/artifact_zip_listing.md` (written by
`_write_container_overhead_md` in `c2.py`). The new `container_overhead` field
on factorial rows (added in `factorial_row`) records the per-entry
`zipfile.infolist()` for each saved artifact, including the inner zip entries.

**No data was removed from the artifacts** — the nested zip is needed to run
the quantized model (it carries the qparams, packed weights, and module
structure). The explanation is in `results/partc_summary.md` (section
"Container overhead").

## 5. C2 explanation correction (UF_HIDDEN)

C2_DONE.md (immutable) attributes the `pip install -e .` failure to a
`#`-comment issue in the `.pth` file. **The real cause:** `uv venv --seed`
writes the site-packages `.pth` files with the macOS `UF_HIDDEN`
(0x80000000) file flag, and CPython's `site.py` (3.12) skips hidden `.pth`
files, so `lab3.pth` was ignored and `import lab3` failed.

This correction is recorded in:
- `results/partc_summary.md` (preamble paragraph)
- `results/SCHEMA.md` (C3 changelog section)

def _rss_subprocess(arch: str, artifact: str, kind: str) -> dict:
    """Fresh-subprocess peak RSS: imports + bench input load -> before;
    artifact load + few forwards -> peak."""
    import json
    import subprocess
    import sys

    code = f"""
import json, psutil, sys
import torch
torch.backends.quantized.engine = "qnnpack"
from lab3.util import set_threads
from lab3.bench import load_bench_input
from lab3.precision import _rebuild_from_artifact, _model_in_dtype
set_threads()
arch = {arch!r}
x, ei = load_bench_input(arch)
proc = psutil.Process()
before = proc.memory_info().rss
m = _rebuild_from_artifact(arch, {artifact!r}, {kind!r})
m.eval()
dtype = _model_in_dtype(m)
peak = before
with torch.inference_mode():
    for _ in range(5):
        if arch == "gcn":
            m(x.to(dtype), ei)
        else:
            m(x[:256].to(dtype))
        peak = max(peak, proc.memory_info().rss)
print(json.dumps({{"before": int(before), "peak": int(peak)}}))
"""
    proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code],
                          capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
                          cwd=str(ROOT),
                          env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": str(ROOT / "code")})
    out = json.loads(proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Artifact save / reload
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _save_artifact(model: nn.Module, path: Path, kind: str, arch: str) -> int:
    """Persist the converted model to `path`. Returns file bytes."""
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    torch.save({"kind": kind,
                "architecture": arch,
                "state": _artifact_state(model, kind, arch)}, path)
    return os.path.getsize(path)


def _container_overhead(path: str) -> dict:
    """C3: per-entry `zipfile.infolist()` accounting of a saved artifact, so the
    container overhead (artifact_bytes - payload_bytes) is attributable instead
    of "unexplained".

    For every artifact torch.save writes a zip. The zip's local headers +
    central-directory + EOCD are `structural_bytes`; the sum of `file_size`
    across entries is `stored_bytes`; for int8_dynamic/int8_static the state
    is `{"pickled": <nested torch.save zip bytes>}`, so the outer data.pkl
    embeds the ENTIRE inner zip as one stored (uncompressed) blob — that blob
    is itself a zip (with its own structural bytes + data entries). We unpack
    that inner zip too (`inner`), so the reader can see that the "overhead" on
    the mlp/gcn int8 rows is the nested re-encoding, not dead data.

    Returns {artifact_bytes, structural_bytes, stored_bytes, entries: [...],
             inner: {structural_bytes, stored_bytes, entries: [...]} | None}.
    """
    import io as _io
    info = zipfile.ZipFile(path).infolist()
    out = {
        "artifact_bytes": os.path.getsize(path),
        "structural_bytes": int(os.path.getsize(path) - sum(i.file_size for i in info)),
        "stored_bytes": int(sum(i.file_size for i in info)),
        "entries": [{"name": i.filename, "file_size": i.file_size,
                     "compress_size": i.compress_size,
                     "compress_type": i.compress_type} for i in info],
        "inner": None,
    }
    try:
        payload = torch.load(path, weights_only=False)
        st = (payload or {}).get("state") or {}
        if isinstance(st, dict) and "pickled" in st:
            zi = zipfile.ZipFile(_io.BytesIO(st["pickled"]))
            in_info = zi.infolist()
            out["inner"] = {
                "stored_bytes": int(sum(i.file_size for i in in_info)),
                "structural_bytes": int(len(st["pickled"]) - sum(i.file_size for i in in_info)),
                "entries": [{"name": i.filename, "file_size": i.file_size,
                             "compress_size": i.compress_size,
                             "compress_type": i.compress_type} for i in in_info],
            }
    except Exception:
        pass
    return out


def _artifact_state(model: nn.Module, kind: str, arch: str) -> dict:
    if kind == "int4_simulated":
        flat = {}
        for name, m_ in model.named_modules():
            if isinstance(m_, (Int4PackedLinear, Int4PackedConv)):
                for k, v in m_.state_dict().items():
                    flat[f"{name}.{k}"] = v
        # Also save the fp32 parent weights so the reload can rebuild the
        # base model with the correct shapes before wrapping.
        fp32 = {}
        for name, m_ in model.named_modules():
            if not isinstance(m_, (Int4PackedLinear, Int4PackedConv)):
                for k, v in m_.state_dict().items():
                    if torch.is_tensor(v) and v.is_floating_point():
                        fp32[f"{name}.{k}"] = v
        return {"packed": flat, "fp32": fp32}
    if kind in ("fp16", "bf16"):
        return {k: v for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
    if kind == "fp32":
        # Plain fp32 model (dense or sparse): store the full state dict.
        return {k: v for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}

def _classify(e: Exception) -> str:
    msg = str(e)
    if "NoQEngine" in msg or "Didn't find engine" in msg:
        return f"unsupported_backend: {type(e).__name__}: {msg[:120]}"
    if "NotImplementedError" in type(e).__name__ or "Could not run" in msg:
        return f"unsupported_op: {type(e).__name__}: {msg[:120]}"
    if "deprecated" in msg.lower():
        return f"deprecated_api: {type(e).__name__}: {msg[:120]}"
    return f"{type(e).__name__}: {msg[:120]}"


def _serialize_and_reload(rec: dict, model: nn.Module, arch: str, kind: str,
                          tolerance: float) -> None:
    """Save the converted artifact, reload it, and compare logits on a fixed
    input slice (reload_equivalence). C2: also records bytes_by_dtype (the
    sum of numel*element_size per stored dtype) next to artifact_bytes so the
    container overhead (artifact_bytes - sum(bytes_by_dtype.values())) is
    visible, and the integer-representation nonzero count."""
    PRECISION_ARTIFACT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = PRECISION_ARTIFACT_DIR / f"{arch}-{rec['method']}_{rec['run_id']}.pt"
    rec["artifact"] = str(path)
    rec["artifact_bytes"] = _save_artifact(model, path, kind, arch)
    bbd = bytes_by_dtype(model, kind)
    rec["bytes_by_dtype"] = bbd
    rec["payload_bytes"] = int(sum(bbd.values()))
    reloaded = _rebuild_from_artifact(arch, str(path), kind)
    x, ei = load_bench_input(arch)
    if arch == "gcn":
        lx, lei = x, ei
    else:
        lx, lei = x[:16], None
    a = logits_of(model, arch, lx, lei)
    b = logits_of(reloaded, arch, lx, lei)
    max_diff = float((a - b).abs().max())
    rec["reload_equivalence"] = {"tolerance": tolerance,
                                 "max_abs_diff": max_diff,
                                 "passed": bool(max_diff <= tolerance)}

def logits_of(model: nn.Module, arch: str, x, ei) -> torch.Tensor:
    model.eval()
    in_dtype = _model_in_dtype(model)
    with torch.inference_mode():

PRECISION_ARTIFACT_DIR = RESULTS_DIR / "precision_artifacts"


def _row(arch: str, phase: str, method: str, parent_run_id: str) -> dict:
    rec = base_record(arch, command="eval")
    rec.update({
        "part": "C",
        "phase": phase,
        "method": method,
        "parent_run_id": parent_run_id,
        "frac_macs_reduced_precision": None,
        "reload_equivalence": None,
        "runtime_status": "ok",
        "calibration": None,
        "reduced_precision_ops": [],
    })
    return rec


def run_wall(rec: dict, t0: float) -> dict:
    rec["wall_time_s"] = round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3)
    return rec


def _classify(e: Exception) -> str:
    msg = str(e)
    if "NoQEngine" in msg or "Didn't find engine" in msg:
        return f"unsupported_backend: {type(e).__name__}: {msg[:120]}"
    if "NotImplementedError" in type(e).__name__ or "Could not run" in msg:
        return f"unsupported_op: {type(e).__name__}: {msg[:120]}"
    if "deprecated" in msg.lower():
        return f"deprecated_api: {type(e).__name__}: {msg[:120]}"
    return f"{type(e).__name__}: {msg[:120]}"


def _serialize_and_reload(rec: dict, model: nn.Module, arch: str, kind: str,
                          tolerance: float) -> None:
    """Save the converted artifact, reload it, and compare logits on a fixed
    input slice (reload_equivalence). C2: also records bytes_by_dtype (the
    sum of numel*element_size per stored dtype) next to artifact_bytes so the
    container overhead (artifact_bytes - sum(bytes_by_dtype.values())) is
    visible, and the integer-representation nonzero count."""
    PRECISION_ARTIFACT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = PRECISION_ARTIFACT_DIR / f"{arch}-{rec['method']}_{rec['run_id']}.pt"
    rec["artifact"] = str(path)
    rec["artifact_bytes"] = _save_artifact(model, path, kind, arch)
    bbd = bytes_by_dtype(model, kind)
    rec["bytes_by_dtype"] = bbd
    rec["payload_bytes"] = int(sum(bbd.values()))
    reloaded = _rebuild_from_artifact(arch, str(path), kind)
    x, ei = load_bench_input(arch)
    if arch == "gcn":
        lx, lei = x, ei
    else:
        lx, lei = x[:16], None
    a = logits_of(model, arch, lx, lei)
    b = logits_of(reloaded, arch, lx, lei)
    max_diff = float((a - b).abs().max())
    rec["reload_equivalence"] = {"tolerance": tolerance,
                                 "max_abs_diff": max_diff,
                                 "passed": bool(max_diff <= tolerance)}

def select_int8(arch: str, parent: nn.Module, parent_run_id: str,
                dyn_rec: dict, stat_rec: dict) -> dict:
    """Select the best supported INT8 method for `arch` by the frozen C.1
    rule: higher validation accuracy; ties within one val example -> lower
    batch-256 (fmnist) / full-graph (gcn) median latency. If only one method
    is supported, use it."""
    lat_key = "full_graph" if arch == "gcn" else "batch_256"

    def _val_count(rec: dict) -> int:
        n_val = 500 if arch == "gcn" else 5000
        return int(round(rec["val_acc"] * n_val))

    def _lat(rec: dict) -> float | None:
        d = (rec.get("latency") or {}).get(lat_key) or {}
        v = d.get("median_ms")
        return float(v) if isinstance(v, (int, float)) else None

    candidates = []
    for name, rec in (("int8_dynamic", dyn_rec), ("int8_static", stat_rec)):
        if rec.get("status") != "ok" or rec.get("val_acc") is None:
            continue
        candidates.append((name, rec))

    if not candidates:
        return {"arch": arch, "selected": None,
                "reason": "no supported INT8 method", "candidates": []}
    if len(candidates) == 1:
        sel_name, sel_rec = candidates[0]
        return {"arch": arch, "selected": sel_name,
                "val_acc": sel_rec["val_acc"],
                "latency_ms": _lat(sel_rec),
                "run_id": sel_rec["run_id"],
                "reason": "only one method supported",
                "candidates": [(n, r["val_acc"], _lat(r), r["run_id"]) for n, r in candidates]}

    # Both supported: higher val accuracy wins; tie within 1 example -> lower latency
    (n1, r1), (n2, r2) = candidates
    c1, c2 = _val_count(r1), _val_count(r2)
    if abs(c1 - c2) <= 1:
        l1, l2 = _lat(r1), _lat(r2)
        if l1 is not None and l2 is not None:
            sel = (n1, r1) if l1 <= l2 else (n2, r2)
        else:
            sel = (n1, r1)  # default to dynamic if latency missing
    else:
        sel = (n1, r1) if c1 > c2 else (n2, r2)
    return {"arch": arch, "selected": sel[0],
            "val_acc": sel[1]["val_acc"],
            "latency_ms": _lat(sel[1]),
            "run_id": sel[1]["run_id"],
            "reason": f"val count {c1} vs {c2}; "
                      f"latency {_lat(r1)} vs {_lat(r2)} ms",
            "candidates": [(n, r["val_acc"], _lat(r), r["run_id"]) for n, r in candidates]}

def _load_sparse_checkpoint(arch: str, pilot_arm_id: str) -> tuple[nn.Module, dict]:
    """Load the sparse seed-0 pilot checkpoint selected by partc_selection.json."""
    from .prune import PILOT_DIR
    path = PILOT_DIR / f"{pilot_arm_id}.pt"
    payload = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    m = build_model(arch)
    m.load_state_dict(payload["state_dict"])
    m.eval()
    return m, payload


def factorial_row(arch: str, condition: str, model: nn.Module,
                  parent_run_id: str, kind: str, parent: nn.Module,
                  write: bool = True, nonzero_count: int | None = None,
                  src_fp32: nn.Module | None = None) -> dict:
    """One factorial row (12 conditions: 3 archs x 4 conditions).

    condition in {"dense_fp32", "sparse_fp32", "dense_int8", "sparse_int8"}.
    `kind` is the artifact format for save/reload ("fp32" for the two fp32
    conditions, or "int8_dynamic"/"int8_static" for the two int8 conditions).
    `parent` is a plain fp32 model with the same op structure (used only for
    the per-op MAC table; for dense rows it is the model itself, for sparse
    rows it is the dense parent — MACs are shape-based and identical)."""
    set_threads()
    set_qnnpack_engine()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rec = _row(arch, "factorial", condition, parent_run_id)
    try:
        va_acc, va_loss, te_acc, te_loss = eval_model(model, arch, condition)
        rec["val_acc"] = va_acc
        rec["val_loss"] = va_loss
        rec["test_acc"] = te_acc

        # size fields: nonzero_count is the model's source (fp32) nonzero
        # weight count (quantization preserves the zero pattern); default to
        # model.parameters() when the model has real parameters (fp32 rows).
        rec["total_params"] = count_params(parent)
        if nonzero_count is not None:
            rec["nonzero_params"] = nonzero_count
        else:
            rec["nonzero_params"] = sum(int(p.count_nonzero()) for p in model.parameters())
        # C2: nonzero count of the INTEGER weight representation. For int8
        # conditions this is the nonzero count of the quantized int8 weights
        # (int_repr), which for dense is == the dense-parent nonzero count and
        # for sparse is the count of surviving nonzero weights after INT8
        # (evidence for whether zeros survive quantization). For fp32
        # conditions it equals the fp32 param nonzero count.
        if "int8" in condition:
            rec["nonzero_before_int8"] = nonzero_count
            rec["nonzero_after_int8"] = int8_nonzero(model)
        else:
            rec["nonzero_before_int8"] = rec["nonzero_params"]
            rec["nonzero_after_int8"] = rec["nonzero_params"]

        # latency
        rec["latency"] = _time_model(model, arch)

        # artifact save + RSS + reload equivalence
        PRECISION_ARTIFACT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path = PRECISION_ARTIFACT_DIR / f"{arch}-{condition}_{rec['run_id']}.pt"
        rec["artifact"] = str(path)
        rec["artifact_bytes"] = _save_artifact(model, path, kind, arch)
        bbd = bytes_by_dtype(model, kind)
        rec["bytes_by_dtype"] = bbd
        rec["payload_bytes"] = int(sum(bbd.values()))
        # C3: per-entry container-overhead accounting (zipfile infolist), so the
        # "unexplained" dense-vs-sparse artifact_bytes gap (issue 2) is visible
        # instead of hidden. For int8 (state = {"pickled": <nested torch.save
        # zip bytes>}) the outer data.pkl embeds the whole inner zip as one
        # stored (uncompressed) blob, so outer overhead >> inner; for fp32 and
        # cnn-static-int8 (state = state_dict) the overhead is a few KB.
        rec["container_overhead"] = _container_overhead(str(path))
        rss = _rss_subprocess(arch, rec["artifact"], kind)
        rec["rss_before_model_bytes"] = rss["before"]
        rec["peak_rss_bytes"] = rss["peak"]
        rec["model_rss_delta_bytes"] = rss["peak"] - rss["before"]

        tol = 0.0 if kind == "fp32" else 1e-3

        a = logits_of(model, arch, lx, lei)
        b = logits_of(reloaded, arch, lx, lei)
        max_diff = float((a - b).abs().max())
        rec["reload_equivalence"] = {"tolerance": tol,
                                     "max_abs_diff": max_diff,
                                     "passed": bool(max_diff <= tol)}

        # per-layer table + frac_macs (MACs from the fp32 `parent` structure)
        x, ei = load_bench_input(arch)
        parent_ops = eligible_ops(parent)
        mac_table = _weight_macs(parent, x, ei)
        mac_by_name = {t["name"]: t for t in mac_table}
        if "int8" in condition:
            red_set = _int8_reduced_names(model, arch, parent)
            rec["stored_precision"] = "int8 weights (qnnpack)"
            rec["compute_precision"] = "int8 (qnnpack)"
            rec["accumulator_precision"] = "int32 (qnnpack), fp32 dequant"
        else:
            red_set = set()
            rec["stored_precision"] = "fp32"
            rec["compute_precision"] = "fp32"
            rec["accumulator_precision"] = "fp32"

                          "compute_precision": rec["compute_precision"],

        rec["per_layer"] = table

        rec["reduced_precision_ops"] = sorted(red_set)

        if write:

        return rec
    except Exception as e:

def _sparse_int8_storage_bytes(src: nn.Module, arch: str) -> int:
    """Theoretical sparse-INT8 storage size: INT8 values (1 B each nonzero) +
    int32 CSR indices (4 B each) + fp32 scales (4 B per output channel).
    Labelled runtime-unsupported (no sparse INT8 CPU kernel). `src` is the
    source fp32 model (the sparse model before INT8 conversion): the sparsity
    pattern is preserved by quantization, so the storage is computed from the
    fp32 weights."""
    total = 0
    for name, op, kind in eligible_ops(src):
        if kind == "lin":
            op = op.lin if hasattr(op, "lin") else op
        if hasattr(op, "weight") and torch.is_tensor(op.weight):
            w = op.weight
        else:
            continue
        nnz = int(w.count_nonzero())
        out_ch = w.shape[0]
        total += nnz * 1          # int8 values
        total += nnz * 4          # int32 CSR column indices
        total += (nnz + out_ch) * 4  # int32 indptr + fp32 scales
    return total

def factorial_row(arch: str, condition: str, model: nn.Module,
                  parent_run_id: str, kind: str, parent: nn.Module,
                  write: bool = True, nonzero_count: int | None = None,

    `kind` is the artifact format for save/reload ("fp32" for the two fp32
    conditions, or "int8_dynamic"/"int8_static" for the two int8 conditions).
    `parent` is a plain fp32 model with the same op structure (used only for
    the per-op MAC table; for dense rows it is the model itself, for sparse
    rows it is the dense parent — MACs are shape-based and identical)."""
    set_threads()
    set_qnnpack_engine()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rec = _row(arch, "factorial", condition, parent_run_id)
    try:
        va_acc, va_loss, te_acc, te_loss = eval_model(model, arch, condition)
        rec["val_acc"] = va_acc
        rec["val_loss"] = va_loss

        # size fields: nonzero_count is the model's source (fp32) nonzero
        # weight count (quantization preserves the zero pattern); default to
        # model.parameters() when the model has real parameters (fp32 rows).
        rec["total_params"] = count_params(parent)
        if nonzero_count is not None:
            rec["nonzero_params"] = nonzero_count
        else:
            rec["nonzero_params"] = sum(int(p.count_nonzero()) for p in model.parameters())
        # C2: nonzero count of the INTEGER weight representation. For int8
        # conditions this is the nonzero count of the quantized int8 weights
        # (int_repr), which for dense is == the dense-parent nonzero count and
        # for sparse is the count of surviving nonzero weights after INT8
        # (evidence for whether zeros survive quantization). For fp32
        # conditions it equals the fp32 param nonzero count.
        if "int8" in condition:
            rec["nonzero_before_int8"] = nonzero_count
            rec["nonzero_after_int8"] = int8_nonzero(model)
        else:
            rec["nonzero_before_int8"] = rec["nonzero_params"]
            rec["nonzero_after_int8"] = rec["nonzero_params"]

        # latency
        rec["latency"] = _time_model(model, arch)

        # artifact save + RSS + reload equivalence
        PRECISION_ARTIFACT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path = PRECISION_ARTIFACT_DIR / f"{arch}-{condition}_{rec['run_id']}.pt"
        rec["artifact"] = str(path)
        rec["artifact_bytes"] = _save_artifact(model, path, kind, arch)
        bbd = bytes_by_dtype(model, kind)
        rec["bytes_by_dtype"] = bbd
        rec["payload_bytes"] = int(sum(bbd.values()))
        # C3: per-entry container-overhead accounting (zipfile infolist), so the
        # "unexplained" dense-vs-sparse artifact_bytes gap (issue 2) is visible
        # instead of hidden. For int8 (state = {"pickled": <nested torch.save
        # zip bytes>}) the outer data.pkl embeds the whole inner zip as one

        # reload equivalence (tolerance 0 for fp32, 1e-3 for int8)
        tol = 0.0 if kind == "fp32" else 1e-3
        reloaded = _rebuild_from_artifact(arch, str(path), kind)
        x, ei = load_bench_input(arch)
        lx, lei = (x, ei) if arch == "gcn" else (x[:16], None)
        a = logits_of(model, arch, lx, lei)
        b = logits_of(reloaded, arch, lx, lei)
        max_diff = float((a - b).abs().max())
        rec["reload_equivalence"] = {"tolerance": tol,
                                     "max_abs_diff": max_diff,
                                     "passed": bool(max_diff <= tol)}

        # per-layer table + frac_macs (MACs from the fp32 `parent` structure)
        x, ei = load_bench_input(arch)
        parent_ops = eligible_ops(parent)
        mac_table = _weight_macs(parent, x, ei)
        mac_by_name = {t["name"]: t for t in mac_table}
        if "int8" in condition:
            red_set = _int8_reduced_names(model, arch, parent)
            rec["stored_precision"] = "int8 weights (qnnpack)"
            rec["compute_precision"] = "int8 (qnnpack)"
            rec["accumulator_precision"] = "int32 (qnnpack), fp32 dequant"
        else:
            red_set = set()
            rec["stored_precision"] = "fp32"
            rec["compute_precision"] = "fp32"
            rec["accumulator_precision"] = "fp32"
        table = []
        for name, _op, kind_ in parent_ops:
            row_t = mac_by_name.get(name)
            if row_t is None:
                continue
            table.append({"name": name, "type": kind_, "macs": row_t["macs"],
                          "stored_precision": rec["stored_precision"],
                          "compute_precision": rec["compute_precision"],
                          "reduced_precision": bool(name in red_set)})
        rec["per_layer"] = table
        rec["frac_macs_reduced_precision"] = frac_macs_reduced_precision(parent, arch, red_set)
        rec["reduced_precision_ops"] = sorted(red_set)

        # sparse fields
        if "sparse" in condition:
            # storage from the source fp32 sparse model (sparsity preserved)
            src = src_fp32 if src_fp32 is not None else model
            if "int8" in condition:
                rec["sparse_int8_storage_bytes"] = _sparse_int8_storage_bytes(src, arch)
                rec["sparse_int8_runtime_status"] = "runtime_unsupported"

        rec = run_wall(rec, t0)
        if write:
            write_run_record(rec)
        return rec
    except Exception as e:
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        rec["status"] = "failed"
        rec["reason"] = _classify(e)
        rec = run_wall(rec, t0)
        if write:
            write_run_record(rec)
        raise

def select_int8(arch: str, parent: nn.Module, parent_run_id: str,
                dyn_rec: dict, stat_rec: dict) -> dict:
    """Select the best supported INT8 method for `arch` by the frozen C.1
    rule: higher validation accuracy; ties within one val example -> lower
    batch-256 (fmnist) / full-graph (gcn) median latency. If only one method
    is supported, use it."""
    lat_key = "full_graph" if arch == "gcn" else "batch_256"

    def _val_count(rec: dict) -> int:
        n_val = 500 if arch == "gcn" else 5000
        return int(round(rec["val_acc"] * n_val))

    def _lat(rec: dict) -> float | None:
        d = (rec.get("latency") or {}).get(lat_key) or {}
        v = d.get("median_ms")
        return float(v) if isinstance(v, (int, float)) else None

    candidates = []
    for name, rec in (("int8_dynamic", dyn_rec), ("int8_static", stat_rec)):
        if rec.get("status") != "ok" or rec.get("val_acc") is None:
            continue
        candidates.append((name, rec))

    if not candidates:
        return {"arch": arch, "selected": None,
                "reason": "no supported INT8 method", "candidates": []}
    if len(candidates) == 1:
        sel_name, sel_rec = candidates[0]
        return {"arch": arch, "selected": sel_name,
                "val_acc": sel_rec["val_acc"],
                "latency_ms": _lat(sel_rec),
                "run_id": sel_rec["run_id"],
                "reason": "only one method supported",
                "candidates": [(n, r["val_acc"], _lat(r), r["run_id"]) for n, r in candidates]}

    # Both supported: higher val accuracy wins; tie within 1 example -> lower latency
    (n1, r1), (n2, r2) = candidates
    c1, c2 = _val_count(r1), _val_count(r2)
    if abs(c1 - c2) <= 1:
        l1, l2 = _lat(r1), _lat(r2)
        if l1 is not None and l2 is not None:
            sel = (n1, r1) if l1 <= l2 else (n2, r2)
        else:
            sel = (n1, r1)  # default to dynamic if latency missing
    else:
        sel = (n1, r1) if c1 > c2 else (n2, r2)
    return {"arch": arch, "selected": sel[0],
            "val_acc": sel[1]["val_acc"],
            "latency_ms": _lat(sel[1]),
            "run_id": sel[1]["run_id"],
            "reason": f"val count {c1} vs {c2}; "
                      f"latency {_lat(r1)} vs {_lat(r2)} ms",
            "candidates": [(n, r["val_acc"], _lat(r), r["run_id"]) for n, r in candidates]}

"""Part C (reduced precision) C2 drivers.

Moved into the package from the standalone ``code/lab3_precision.py`` module
(deleted per C2 item 7) so the study is driven via:

    uv run python -m lab3 precision
    uv run python -m lab3 factorial

Per predictions.md C.1 / C.2 / C.3:
  results/runs.jsonl          phase="precision" rows (5 formats x 3 archs)
  results/int8_selection.json INT8 method selection per architecture
  results/factorial.csv       12-condition factorial
  results/precision_artifacts/<arch>-<method>_<run_id>.pt
  results/partc_summary.md    (written by the summary step)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json

import torch

from .util import RESULTS_DIR, code_hash, set_threads
from .evaln import load_checkpoint
from .prune import PILOT_DIR
from . import precision as P

ARCHS = ("mlp", "cnn", "gcn")
FORMATS = ("fp16", "bf16", "int8_dynamic", "int8_static", "int4_simulated")


def partc_selection() -> dict:
    p = RESULTS_DIR / "partc_selection.json"
    return json.load(open(p))


def _parent_run_id(arch: str) -> str:
    """Look up the seed-0 dense Part A run id for the architecture."""
    runs = [json.loads(ln) for ln in (RESULTS_DIR / "runs.jsonl").read_text().splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    for r in runs:
        if (r.get("architecture") == arch
                and r.get("seed") == 0
                and r.get("method") == "dense"
                and (r.get("part") == "A" or r.get("phase") is None)
                and r.get("val_acc") is not None):
            return r["run_id"]
    return "dense_seed0"


def dense_parent(arch: str) -> torch.nn.Module:
    parent, _ = load_checkpoint(arch, 0)
    parent.eval()
    return parent


def run_precision(arch: str | None = None) -> list:
    archs = (arch,) if arch else ARCHS
    out = []
    set_threads()
    P.set_qnnpack_engine()
    for a in archs:
        parent = dense_parent(a)
        prid = _parent_run_id(a)
        for fmt in FORMATS:
            print(f"[precision] {a} {fmt}", flush=True)
            rec = P.convert_and_measure(a, fmt, parent, prid, write=True)
            print(f"   status={rec.get('status')} val_acc={rec.get('val_acc')} "
                  f"nonzero={rec.get('nonzero_params')} "
                  f"frac_macs={rec.get('frac_macs_reduced_precision')} "
                  f"artifact_bytes={rec.get('artifact_bytes')} "
                  f"reload={rec.get('reload_equivalence')}", flush=True)
            out.append(rec)
    return out


def run_int8_selection(arch: str | None = None) -> dict:
    archs = (arch,) if arch else ARCHS
    out = {}
    set_threads()
    P.set_qnnpack_engine()
    for a in archs:
        parent = dense_parent(a)
        prid = _parent_run_id(a)
        print(f"[int8_selection] {a}", flush=True)
        dyn_rec = P.convert_and_measure(a, "int8_dynamic", parent, prid, write=False)
        stat_rec = P.convert_and_measure(a, "int8_static", parent, prid, write=False)
        out[a] = P.select_int8(a, parent, prid, dyn_rec, stat_rec)
        print(f"   selected={out[a].get('selected')} reason={out[a].get('reason')}", flush=True)
    return out


def run_int8_rerun(arch: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """C3: re-run ONLY the INT8 records as new rows (the C2 int8 rows are
    superseded because their integer-weight accounting was blind to the
    quantized projection weights). Re-runs:
      - standalone int8_dynamic + int8_static for each arch (phase="precision");
      - dense_int8 + sparse_int8 factorial conditions for each arch
        (phase="factorial", using the C2-selected int8 method per arch from
        int8_selection.json).
    Returns {"precision": [...], "factorial": [...], "selection": {...}}.
    The selection is recomputed from the NEW precision rows; the caller writes
    it to results/int8_selection.json.
    """
    archs = (arch,) if arch else ARCHS
    prec_out = []
    fact_out = []
    sel_out = {}
    set_threads()
    P.set_qnnpack_engine()
    sel_path = RESULTS_DIR / "int8_selection.json"
    for a in archs:
        parent = dense_parent(a)
        prid = _parent_run_id(a)
        # Standalone int8_dynamic + int8_static (phase="precision").
        dyn_rec = P.convert_and_measure(a, "int8_dynamic", parent, prid, write=True)
        stat_rec = P.convert_and_measure(a, "int8_static", parent, prid, write=True)
        prec_out.extend([dyn_rec, stat_rec])
        # Recompute selection from the new precision rows.
        sel_out[a] = P.select_int8(a, parent, prid, dyn_rec, stat_rec)
        int8_method = sel_out[a].get("selected", "int8_dynamic")
        quant = (P.int8_quantize_dynamic if int8_method == "int8_dynamic"
                 else P.int8_quantize_static)
        # Factorial dense_int8 + sparse_int8 (phase="factorial").
        pcsel = partc_selection()[a]
        sparse_arm = pcsel["selected"]["pilot_arm_id"]
        sparse_model, _ = _load_sparse_checkpoint(a, sparse_arm)
        sparse_model.eval()
        dense_q, _ = quant(parent, a)
        sparse_q, _ = quant(sparse_model, a)
        dense_nn = sum(int(p.count_nonzero()) for p in parent.parameters())
        sparse_nn = sum(int(p.count_nonzero()) for p in sparse_model.parameters())
        for cond, model, nnz, src in (("dense_int8", dense_q, dense_nn, parent),
                                      ("sparse_int8", sparse_q, sparse_nn, sparse_model)):
            print(f"[int8_rerun] {a} {cond} ({int8_method})", flush=True)
            rec = P.factorial_row(a, cond, model, prid, int8_method, src,
                                  write=True, nonzero_count=nnz, src_fp32=parent)
            print(f"   status={rec.get('status')} val_acc={rec.get('val_acc')} "
                  f"nonzero_after_int8={rec.get('nonzero_after_int8')} "
                  f"artifact_bytes={rec.get('artifact_bytes')} "
                  f"bytes_by_dtype={rec.get('bytes_by_dtype')}", flush=True)
            fact_out.append(rec)
    return {"precision": prec_out, "factorial": fact_out, "selection": sel_out}


def _load_sparse_checkpoint(arch: str, pilot_arm_id: str) -> tuple[torch.nn.Module, dict]:
    """Load the sparse seed-0 pilot checkpoint selected by partc_selection.json."""
    path = PILOT_DIR / f"{pilot_arm_id}.pt"
    payload = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    m = P.build_model(arch)
    m.load_state_dict(payload["state_dict"])
    m.eval()
    return m, payload


def run_factorial(arch: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    archs = (arch,) if arch else ARCHS
    set_threads()
    P.set_qnnpack_engine()
    sel = partc_selection()
    rows = []
    for a in archs:
        parent = dense_parent(a)
        prid = _parent_run_id(a)
        sparse_arm = sel[a]["selected"]["pilot_arm_id"]
        sparse_model, _ = _load_sparse_checkpoint(a, sparse_arm)
        sparse_model.eval()
        # The INT8 method to apply is the one SELECTED by the frozen C.2 rule
        # (recomputed from the new precision rows -> results/int8_selection.json).
        import json as _json
        sel_path = RESULTS_DIR / "int8_selection.json"
        if sel_path.exists():
            with open(sel_path) as f:
                sel2 = _json.load(f)["selection"]
            int8_method = sel2[a]["selected"]
        else:
            int8_method = "int8_dynamic"
        quant = (P.int8_quantize_dynamic if int8_method == "int8_dynamic"
                 else P.int8_quantize_static)
        dense_q, _ = quant(parent, a)
        sparse_q, _ = quant(sparse_model, a)
        dense_nn = sum(int(p.count_nonzero()) for p in parent.parameters())
        sparse_nn = sum(int(p.count_nonzero()) for p in sparse_model.parameters())
        conditions = [
            ("dense_fp32", parent, "fp32", dense_nn, parent),
            ("sparse_fp32", sparse_model, "fp32", sparse_nn, sparse_model),
            ("dense_int8", dense_q, int8_method, dense_nn, parent),
            ("sparse_int8", sparse_q, int8_method, sparse_nn, sparse_model),
        ]
        for cond, model, kind, nnz, src in conditions:
            print(f"[factorial] {a} {cond} (int8={int8_method})", flush=True)
            model.eval()
            rec = P.factorial_row(a, cond, model, prid, kind, parent,
                                  write=True, nonzero_count=nnz, src_fp32=src)
            rows.append(rec)
    return rows


def run_int8_selection_and_factorial(arch: str | None = None) -> None:
    """INT8 selection (writes results/int8_selection.json) + 12-condition
    factorial (writes results/factorial.csv). Both run from the C2 precision
    rows; the INT8 method applied to the factorial is the selected one."""
    sel = run_int8_selection(arch)
    archs = (arch,) if arch else ARCHS
    # Merge into any existing selection file (keeps all three archs if a
    # single arch is rerun).
    sel_path = RESULTS_DIR / "int8_selection.json"
    merged: dict = {}
    if sel_path.exists():
        try:
            merged = json.load(open(sel_path)).get("selection", {})
        except Exception:
            merged = {}
    merged.update(sel)
    with open(sel_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump({"code": code_hash(), "selection": merged}, f, indent=1)
    print(f"[int8_selection] wrote {sel_path}", flush=True)

    rows = run_factorial(arch)
    _write_factorial_csv(rows)
    print(f"[factorial] wrote {len(rows)} rows to results/factorial.csv", flush=True)


def _write_factorial_csv(rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    import csv
    fieldnames = ["part", "phase", "method", "architecture", "val_acc", "test_acc",
                  "total_params", "nonzero_params", "nonzero_before_int8",
                  "nonzero_after_int8", "frac_macs_reduced_precision",
                  "reduced_precision_ops", "artifact_bytes", "bytes_by_dtype",
                  "reload_equivalence", "latency", "status", "run_id"]
    with open(RESULTS_DIR / "factorial.csv", "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames, extrasaction="ignore")
        w.writeheader()
        for r in rows:
            rr = dict(r)
            rr["bytes_by_dtype"] = json.dumps(rr.get("bytes_by_dtype"))
            rr["reduced_precision_ops"] = "|".join(rr.get("reduced_precision_ops") or [])
            w.writerow(rr)


def _write_container_overhead_md(rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    """C3: write results/artifact_zip_listing.md — per-entry zipfile.infolist()
    for the 12 latest-ok factorial artifacts, from each row's
    `container_overhead` field (so it reflects the actual saved files)."""
    out = []
    out.append("# Factorial artifact zip listings (C3)\n")
    out.append("Per-entry `zipfile.ZipFile(artifact).infolist()` for the 12 latest-ok\n")
    out.append("3.12 factorial artifacts. `file_size` = stored (uncompressed) bytes;\n")
    out.append("`compress_size` = bytes on disk; `compress_type` 0 = stored (no\n")
    out.append("compression). `OUT` entries are the outer .pt zip (torch.save of\n")
    out.append("`{kind, architecture, state}`); `IN` entries are the inner zip of the\n")
    out.append("`state['pickled']` bytes for the mlp/gcn int8 rows (torch.save(model)\n")
    out.append("re-archives the whole module tree; for cnn static the state is a flat\n")
    out.append("state dict, so there is no inner zip). See C3_DONE.md issue 2 for the\n")
    out.append("explanation of the dense-vs-sparse artifact_bytes gap.\n")
    for arch in ("mlp", "cnn", "gcn"):
        arch_rows = [r for r in rows if r.get("architecture") == arch]
        for cond in ("dense_fp32", "sparse_fp32", "dense_int8", "sparse_int8"):
            row = next((r for r in arch_rows if r.get("method") == cond and r.get("status") == "ok"), None)
            if row is None:
                continue
            co = row.get("container_overhead")
            # C3: the fp32 rows were written by C2 (no container_overhead field).
            # Compute it on the fly from the artifact path so the listing is
            # complete for all 12 conditions.
            if co is None and row.get("artifact"):
                try:
                    from .precision import _container_overhead
                    co = _container_overhead(row["artifact"])
                except Exception:
                    co = {}
            co = co or {}
            out.append(f"## {arch} {cond}  ({row.get('run_id')})\n")
            out.append(f"artifact_bytes = {co.get('artifact_bytes')}; "
                       f"payload_bytes = {row.get('payload_bytes')}; "
                       f"outer structural = {co.get('structural_bytes')}; "
                       f"outer stored = {co.get('stored_bytes')}\n")
            out.append("| entry | file_size | compress_size | compress_type |")
            out.append("|---|---|---|---|")
            for e in co.get("entries", []):
                out.append(f"| OUT {e['name']} | {e['file_size']} | {e['compress_size']} | {e['compress_type']} |")
            if co.get("inner"):
                out.append(f"| (inner zip) stored={co['inner']['stored_bytes']} structural={co['inner']['structural_bytes']} | | | |")
                for e in co["inner"]["entries"]:
                    out.append(f"| IN {e['name']} | {e['file_size']} | {e['compress_size']} | {e['compress_type']} |")
            out.append("")
    (RESULTS_DIR / "artifact_zip_listing.md").write_text("\n".join(out) + "\n")
    print(f"[summary] wrote {RESULTS_DIR / 'artifact_zip_listing.md'}", flush=True)


def write_summary() -> None:
    """Write results/partc_summary.md from the C2 (python 3.12) run rows."""
    runs = [json.loads(ln) for ln in (RESULTS_DIR / "runs.jsonl").read_text().splitlines() if ln.strip()]

    def c2(r: dict) -> bool:
        py = (r.get("versions") or {}).get("python", "")
        return py.startswith("3.12")

    prec_rows: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    fact_rows: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for r in runs:
        if r.get("part") != "C" or not c2(r):
            continue
        if r.get("phase") == "precision":
            prec_rows.setdefault(r.get("architecture"), []).append(r)
        if r.get("phase") == "factorial":
            fact_rows.setdefault(r.get("architecture"), []).append(r)

    # latest ok row per (arch, fmt) for the standalone table. File order in
    # runs.jsonl == write order, so "last ok wins" naturally picks the C3 int8
    # rows over the superseded C2 int8 rows (C3 is written after C2).
    def latest_ok(rows: list[dict]) -> dict[str, dict]:
        out: dict[str, dict] = {}
        for r in rows:
            if r.get("status") == "ok":
                out[r["method"]] = r  # last ok per method wins
        return out

    out = []
    out.append("# Part C (C3) summary\n")
    out.append("Reduced precision: fp16, bf16, dynamic-INT8 (qnnpack), static-INT8 (qnnpack FX), "
               "simulated-INT4, 5 formats x 3 architectures, run on the pinned Python 3.12 "
               "environment (torch 2.15.0). This supersedes the C1b run (Python 3.13 env mismatch) "
               "and the C2 run (2026-11-09/10); the C2 INT8 rows are superseded by C3 because the "
               "C2 integer-weight accounting (`nonzero_after_int8`, `bytes_by_dtype`) was blind to the "
               "quantized projection weights (it only matched modules with a working `_weight_bias`, "
               "missing the FX-static `_packed_weight_N` / raw-ScriptObject shapes — GCN static int8 "
               "reported nonzero_after_int8=23 and bytes_by_dtype={fp32:92}). All 45 C1b and the C2 "
               "part=\"C\" rows are marked superseded in results/ANNOTATIONS.md. Fields: artifact_bytes "
               "+ bytes_by_dtype (per-stored-dtype payload, container overhead = artifact_bytes - "
               "payload_bytes; per-entry zip breakdown in results/artifact_zip_listing.md), "
               "nonzero_params (integer-representation nonzero count), frac_macs_reduced_precision, "
               "latency (batch 1 + batch 256 / full graph, median + IQR), rss, "
               "stored/compute/accumulator precision, reload_equivalence, run_id.\n")
    out.append("C3 also corrects the C2 explanation of the `pip install -e .` failure: the real cause "
               "was that `uv venv --seed` writes the site-packages `.pth` files with the macOS "
               "`UF_HIDDEN` (0x80000000) file flag, and CPython's `site.py` (3.12) skips hidden `.pth` "
               "files, so `lab3.pth` was ignored and `import lab3` failed — NOT the `#`-comment issue "
               "C2_DONE.md described. (C2_DONE.md is immutable; the correction lives here and in "
               "SCHEMA.md's C3 changelog.)\n")

    out.append("## Standalone conversions (phase=\"precision\")\n")
    out.append("| arch | format | val_acc | total_params | nonzero_params | nonzero(dense parent) | "
               "frac_macs | stored | compute | accumulator | artifact_bytes | payload_bytes | bytes_by_dtype | reload max_diff | status | run_id |")
    out.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for arch in ARCHS:
        by_fmt = latest_ok(prec_rows.get(arch, []))
        for fmt in FORMATS:
            r = by_fmt.get(fmt)
            if r is None:
                out.append(f"| {arch} | {fmt} | — (no ok C2 row) | | | | | | | | | | | | | |")
                continue
            re = r.get("reload_equivalence") or {}
            bbd = r.get("bytes_by_dtype") or {}
            out.append(
                f"| {arch} | {fmt} | {r.get('val_acc')} | {r.get('total_params')} | "
                f"{r.get('nonzero_params')} | {r.get('nonzero_params_dense_parent')} | "
                f"{r.get('frac_macs_reduced_precision')} | {r.get('stored_precision')} | "
                f"{r.get('compute_precision')} | {r.get('accumulator_precision')} | "
                f"{r.get('artifact_bytes')} | "
                f"{r.get('payload_bytes')} | {bbd} | {re.get('max_abs_diff')} | "
                f"{r.get('status')} | {r.get('run_id')} |"
            )

    out.append("\n## Latency (median_ms / IQR_ms) and RSS (delta bytes)\n")
    out.append("| arch | format | bs1 med | bs1 IQR | bs256/full med | bs256/full IQR | rss_delta |")
    out.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for arch in ARCHS:
        by_fmt = latest_ok(prec_rows.get(arch, []))
        lkey = "full_graph" if arch == "gcn" else "batch_256"
        bkey = "batch_1"
        for fmt in FORMATS:
            r = by_fmt.get(fmt)
            if r is None:
                continue
            lat = r.get("latency") or {}
            b1 = lat.get(bkey) or {}
            b2 = lat.get(lkey) or {}
            out.append(
                f"| {arch} | {fmt} | {b1.get('median_ms')} | {b1.get('iqr_ms')} | "
                f"{b2.get('median_ms')} | {b2.get('iqr_ms')} | "
                f"{r.get('model_rss_delta_bytes')} |"
            )

    # INT8 selection
    sel_path = RESULTS_DIR / "int8_selection.json"
    out.append("\n## INT8 selection (C.2 rule, C2 run)\n")
    out.append("| arch | selected | val_acc | latency_ms | reason | run_id |")
    out.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    if sel_path.exists():
        sel = json.load(open(sel_path)).get("selection", {})
        for arch in ARCHS:
            s = sel.get(arch, {})
            out.append(f"| {arch} | {s.get('selected')} | {s.get('val_acc')} | "
                       f"{s.get('latency_ms')} | {s.get('reason')} | {s.get('run_id')} |")

    # Factorial — latest ok per (arch, condition) (file order: C3 int8 rows win)
    out.append("\n## 12-condition factorial (phase=\"factorial\", C3 run)\n")
    out.append("| arch | condition | val_acc | total_params | nonzero | nonzero_before_int8 | nonzero_after_int8 | "
               "frac_macs | artifact_bytes | payload_bytes | container_overhead_bytes | reload max_diff | status | run_id |")
    out.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for arch in ARCHS:
        # latest ok per condition
        latest: dict[str, dict] = {}
        for r in fact_rows.get(arch, []):
            if r.get("status") == "ok":
                latest[r.get("method")] = r
        for cond in ("dense_fp32", "sparse_fp32", "dense_int8", "sparse_int8"):
            r = latest.get(cond)
            if r is None:
                continue
            re = r.get("reload_equivalence") or {}
            co = r.get("container_overhead") or {}
            ov = (co.get("artifact_bytes", 0) - (r.get("payload_bytes") or 0)) if co else ""
            out.append(
                f"| {arch} | {r.get('method')} | {r.get('val_acc')} | {r.get('total_params')} | "
                f"{r.get('nonzero_params')} | {r.get('nonzero_before_int8')} | "
                f"{r.get('nonzero_after_int8')} | {r.get('frac_macs_reduced_precision')} | "
                f"{r.get('artifact_bytes')} | {r.get('payload_bytes')} | {ov} | "
                f"{re.get('max_abs_diff')} | {r.get('status')} | {r.get('run_id')} |"
            )

    # Container-overhead explanation (C3 issue 2)
    out.append("\n## Container overhead: why dense and sparse int8 files differ (C3 issue 2)\n")
    out.append("`container_overhead_bytes = artifact_bytes - payload_bytes`. Per-entry breakdowns "

    out.append("- fp32 rows and cnn static-int8: overhead ≈ 3–4 KB (zip structural bytes: 6 outer "
               "entries + central directory + EOCD). The int8 **weight payloads** of dense and sparse "
               "are byte-for-byte the same size (per-tensor int8 is 1 B/weight regardless of the zero "
               "pattern), so dense-vs-sparse file size tracks the fp32-bias/zero-point/scale bytes.\n")
    out.append("- mlp/gcn dynamic- & static-int8: `state = {\"pickled\": <nested torch.save zip bytes>}`. "
               "The outer data.pkl embeds the ENTIRE inner zip as one stored (uncompressed) blob, so the "
               "outer overhead ≈ inner-stored-bytes + inner-structural-bytes. That is why mlp dense_int8 "
               "(359,751 B, payload 236,328 B) shows ≈123 KB overhead while mlp sparse_int8 (260,237 B, "
               "same 236,328 B payload) shows ≈24 KB: the dense inner zip carries the larger fp32 bias "
               "tensors, the sparse inner zip carries the smaller sparse-weight + int8-payload tensors. "
               "It is re-encoding of the same needed data, not dead weight — nothing is removed.\n")

    (RESULTS_DIR / "partc_summary.md").write_text("\n".join(out) + "\n")
    print(f"[summary] wrote {RESULTS_DIR / 'partc_summary.md'}", flush=True)

    # Build the latest-ok factorial rows for the zip listing (same selection as
    # the factorial table above).
    fact_final: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
    for arch in ARCHS:
        for r in fact_rows.get(arch, []):
            if r.get("status") == "ok":

    fact_ordered = [fact_final[(arch, cond)] for arch in ARCHS

    _write_container_overhead_md(fact_ordered)
